coverage_questions: The atlas seed lists Genolator as one configuration, while the paper also documents a projector-only ablation. The ablation is represented separately because its trainability state differs.
The paper documents GPT-4.1 and XGBoost baselines, but they are not listed in the atlas seed; their input routes are therefore not expanded as Genolator trajectories.

The paper does not specify the tokenizer vocabulary or segmentation, the textual-token embedding lookup, the internal architecture of the three projectors beyond a learned linear transformation, or the internal computations of Evo2, EsmFold/ESM-2, and the GCAE.
The paper states mean pooling for three embedding routes, but the pinned catalog has no mean-pooling operation; this is recorded as an operation proposal.

operation_proposals.source_operation: mean pooling along a sequence or node axis
operation_proposals.why_no_existing_operation: Mean pooling aggregates values by arithmetic averaging over a declared axis. Normalization changes scale, projection changes feature space, reshaping changes layout, and concatenation joins values without averaging.

evidence.quote: Genolator is a finetuned multimodal Llama 33-35 model, designed to fuse natural language with genomic  language.  It  receives  a  question,  formulated  in  natural  language  (English),  and information  from  DNA-sequences,  amino  acid  sequences  and  protein  structures  in  tandem.

For each gene's DNA sequence, pertoken embeddings were extracted from the 'blocks.28.mlp.l3' layer, following the model authors' recommendations. These token-level embeddings were then aggregated using mean pooling along the sequence dimension, resulting in a fixed-size 4096-dimensional embedding vector for each gene.

For each token of the sequence, embeddings from the last hidden layer of the ESM-2 block were extracted  and  concatenated,  yielding  per-token  vectors  of  length  2,560.  These  token-level embeddings were aggregated via mean pooling along the sequence dimension, resulting in a single 2,560-dimensional embedding vector per gene.

The corresponding PDB files were first converted to graph  representations  using  Graphein 59 .  These  graphs  were  then  processed  by  the  GCAE, assigning a 128-dimensional embedding to each node. Node embeddings were subsequently aggregated by mean pooling, resulting in a single 128-dimensional embedding vector.

Each projector applied a learnable linear transformation to map the input embedding dimension to  the  hidden  size  expected  by  Llama  (4096).  For  each  sample,  eight virtual tokens per modality were produced, yielding a total of 24 multimodal virtual tokens, which were  concatenated  and  prepended  to  the  textual  input  tokens  for  downstream  model processing.
